clue.text: Barker's timeshare rarely used

definitions.note: a barker is a dog; the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: letters that are used are put to work in a new way, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouting about holiday timeshares that hardly anyone takes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' suggests a fairground tout selling timeshares; it is a dog. The 's is 'is', and 'used' tells you to rearrange TIMESHARE RARELY.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh breed of short-legged terrier is a dog, and dogs are barkers.

clue.text: Reviews ultimately bug poor writer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word reviews

parts.note: its last letter is S
a bug is an insect, a crawler

explanation.surface: Critics' notices finally irritate an author whose work is bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' reads as a verb meaning annoy, but it is a noun: an insect, a crawler.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scrawls writes untidily or badly, hence a poor hand with a pen.

clue.text: Sly character's stealing rector's reading desks

indicators.note: stealing something takes it away, so the rector's letter is removed

parts.note: Sylvester 'Sly' Stallone's best-known character is Rambo; Rambo's gives RAMBOS
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A cunning figure pinches the vicar's lecterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sly' seems to mean cunning, but it is Sylvester Stallone's nickname; his character is Rambo. Take R (rector) away from RAMBOS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised pulpit or lectern in early churches, from which scripture was read.

clue.text: He maybe crosses 25 as passenger when heat's stifling

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one word is enclosed inside the other

parts.note: to sear is to heat fiercely; the 's is 'is'
a fare is a paying passenger, as in a taxi

explanation.surface: A traveller on the Channel crossing feels the heat oppressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-across, the English Channel, which a sailor crosses; 'as' and 'when' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a sailor, who might cross the English Channel by ship.

clue.text: Not alert, a PM's making a U-turn

indicators.note: a U-turn sends the word back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister; Peel's gives PEELS

explanation.surface: A political headline about a sleepy Prime Minister performing a policy U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U-turn' looks like a policy reversal, but here it turns a Victorian PM's name back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is the opposite of alert: dozing and unaware of surroundings.

clue.text: Playing a sexy part, they're continually assessed

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: Actors in a racy role find themselves constantly judged.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests actors being reviewed; the assessment is for tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxpayers are repeatedly assessed by the revenue authorities to fix the tax owed.

clue.text: Wearing skirt to begin with at one Adriatic resort

indicators.note: says that the edge word comes first, ahead of the others

parts.note: to skirt is to border, and a border is a rim
wearing clothes is being in them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Dressed in a skirt, for a start, at an Italian seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' looks like clothing worn, but it means an edge, RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a popular beach town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: One of eight failures in Qatar? Time for a reaction

indicators.note: a chemical reaction rearranges the elements, so these letters are reordered
one thing for another means swapping them, here the letter in place of the a

explanation.surface: A football World Cup in Qatar with eight teams failing, and a time for response.
explanation.walkthrough: Put T (Time) in place of one A in FAILURES IN QATAR, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight teams reach the quarter-finals of a knockout tournament, so a participant there is one of eight.

clue.text: Egghead with book keeping close to picnic hampers

parts.note: the head of egg, its first letter E

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Numbers is a book of the Bible

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, its last letter

parts.note: its last letter is C

explanation.surface: An intellectual, book in hand, minding the picnic baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' looks like picnic baskets; it is the verb. C goes inside NUMBERS, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To encumber is to burden or impede, which is what hampering does.

clue.text: Ladies content to go with you later

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside it, all but its outer letters

parts.note: its inner letters are ADIE
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: Women happy to leave with you at a later time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' is the casual farewell, as in 'Later!'; ADIE comes from inside LADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye; 'later' is informal slang for a parting.

clue.text: Begin with the French getting a lift

parts.note: le is a French word for the
to doff one's hat is to lift it

explanation.surface: Starting with the French catching a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like a ride; it is raising a hat, DOFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to start proceedings, going first.

clue.text: More meaningless twaddle at the end — Truss turning on bank?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter is E

indicators.note: turning round reads the letters backwards

parts.note: Liz Truss was briefly the Prime Minister, a PM
a bank of seats is a tier

explanation.surface: A jibe that Liz Truss turning on the Bank of England was more nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truss' reads as the politician attacking the Bank; she stands for PM, reversed to MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier words have less substance, so they carry less meaning.

clue.text: Green target?

parts.note: on a golf course the putting green has one thing a player aims at

explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests an environmental goal; it is the golf green, where the ball must drop into the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, the hole on each putting green is what every shot is ultimately aimed at.

clue.text: Partner who's gone to pot? Hardly

definitions.text: Partner who's gone to pot? Hardly

parts.words: Partner who's gone to pot? Hardly
parts.note: a pot is slang for a cup or prize, so a spouse won like a prize is far from gone to seed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone to pot' means deteriorated, but a pot is also a trophy; this partner is a glamorous prize, so 'Hardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a young, attractive spouse treated as a status symbol by a wealthy partner.

clue.text: Hopping mad about PM concealing one name — it's personal

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the rest
hopping mad is furious, and hopping jumbles the letters
concealing hides one thing inside another

parts.note: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was a British Prime Minister
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone furious about a Prime Minister hiding a name: it's a personal attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopping mad' is a single idiom, but 'Hopping' alone shuffles the word mad; the PM is Sir Alec Douglas-Home, PM in 1963-64.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad hominem argument attacks the person rather than their case, so it is personal.

clue.text: Angry soldiers locking one rebel leader in tower

indicators.note: locking a prisoner in holds them inside

parts.note: mad means angry
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is R
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Furious troops imprison an insurgent chief in a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, for other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirador is a Spanish watchtower or turret with a view.

clue.text: Boris who had central role in horror show

definitions.text: Boris who had central role in horror show

parts.words: Boris who had central role in horror show
parts.note: points to the actor called Boris who starred in classic horror films

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris' and 'horror show' invite thoughts of Boris Johnson's chaotic government; the Boris meant is the actor who played Frankenstein's monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Karloff starred as the monster in the 1931 film Frankenstein, a horror classic.

clue.text: Vital periods of rest for Spooner and Bones

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: key means vital, essential; said aloud it can be written CEE
naps are short sleeps; said aloud it can be written with a silent K

explanation.surface: Essential breaks from work for an old don and a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY NAPS with its opening sounds swapped becomes 'nee caps', heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneecaps are the patellae, the bones at the front of the knee joints.

clue.text: Phrase regularly repeated by Frost in a Torygraph piece

indicators.note: a piece is a part, a run of letters taken out of these words

explanation.surface: A newspaper column by Frost in the Telegraph, nicknamed the Torygraph, with a stock phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Torygraph is a nickname for the Daily Telegraph, a right-leaning British newspaper; Frost could be broadcaster David Frost.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, an ostinato is a short melodic or rhythmic phrase that is persistently repeated.

clue.text: Coren badly hurt by what intruders did

indicators.note: badly done means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ached means hurt

explanation.surface: A writer named Coren was badly injured by burglars.
explanation.walkthrough: Coren is a well-known British family of writers and broadcasters; rearranged it gives ENCRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Intruders encroached: they trespassed on someone else's territory.

clue.text: Be overfriendly with firms? I agree

parts.note: COS is the plural abbreviation of company
yup is a casual yes

explanation.surface: A question on whether to get too chummy with companies, answered with a yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosy up to someone is to ingratiate yourself with them, being too familiar.

clue.text: Old bloke and kid meeting Spice Girl who's not current

parts.note: to kid is to tease or hoax, which is to cod in British slang

indicators.note: a thing that is not present has been removed

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was a member of the Spice Girls pop group
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An elderly man and a child meet a faded Spice Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb: to cod is to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Codger is informal British for an elderly man, often eccentric.

clue.text: School board sacking head

indicators.note: sacking the head removes the first letter

parts.note: to board a bus is to get on it

explanation.surface: A school's governors fire the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a governing body; it is boarding a vehicle, GET ON, without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Join PM breaking rules? Quite the reverse!

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it
says the roles are swapped: the PM holds the rules instead

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister
R is an abbreviation for rule, so two rules give RR

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Prime Minister broke the rules, then saying the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the rules would go inside the PM; 'Quite the reverse!' flips that, so the PM, Theresa May, holds the rules instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to join two people in wedlock.

clue.text: Withdraw being caught having transgressed again

indicators.note: caught is used here as heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: to transgress is to sin, so having done it again is re-sinned

explanation.surface: A repeat offender caught out and pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like an arrest; it means heard, so re-sinned is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or decision is to revoke or cancel it.

clue.text: Means princess with child has left

parts.note: Princess Anne is the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: A wealthy princess whose child has moved away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like wealth; it is a way of doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel is a medium or route through which something is done, as in proper channels.

clue.text: Get accustomed to duke leaving last

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word is taken out of it

parts.note: to last is to endure

explanation.surface: Getting used to a duke departing at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like the final position; it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To enure, a variant of inure, is to habituate oneself to something unpleasant.

clue.text: Banker could be upset — hears bonus finally scrapped

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged into something else
scrapped means thrown out, so that letter goes from the pool
finally picks the last letter of the word bonus

parts.note: its last letter is S

explanation.surface: A City banker gets upset on hearing that bonuses are cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks. Remove S (end of bonus) from UPSET HEARS and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river of Mesopotamia, and a river flows between banks.
